report:
The unchanged continuation257 manuscript passes as a partial-correctness result in its stated domain. Its reference-moment theorem, intrinsic target criterion, finite-target coercivity estimates, and supporting inequality for already known genuine outputs are established. This does not close original P16.4. General prescribed-target attainment and every-solution equality at every analytic point remain unproved.

I treated only the seven complete O217/D214/N220/T171/Q222/C218/G227 manuscripts and their unchanged clarifications as grants. Their applications retain complete real-valued characteristic/residue-characteristic-zero fields, smooth geometrically integral projective varieties, actual ample rational bundles, raw intersection mass, and arbitrary target support. N remains conditional on its two reference hypotheses. G227 is used as the whole accepted original-field genus-zero endpoint, including nonsplit conics; it supplies no positive-genus theorem. Favorable portions of review198 were not promoted to grants. The task passage below records authorization only and has no external-premise index.

Proposition 1 is correct. On actual P1 with O(1), the sections T1 and a^m T0 generate the bundle and give the displayed continuous FS potential. Its supremum and Gauss-reference value are zero. Q identifies its genuine curvature with the shrinking-disk point mass. Both its value there and its value at z=0 are −ell, whereas its value at the reference atom is zero. O's curve energy formula therefore gives E=−ell/2. For the raw-mass-one target delta_(z=0), the objective is +ell/2 and diverges positively. O's real affine curvature law gives B(tu)=t² ell/2. Taking t=ell^(−1/2) on a sufficiently late tail gives cost 1/2 and target integral sqrt(ell), proving U_mu=∞. Thus M0 alone is insufficient. Adding finite U_mu changes the quantified target scope materially. The revised manuscript retains that condition in every new coercivity and maximizing-cost conclusion. Whole198 remains FAIL as supplied; its report and unresolved source-premise14/15 route gaps remain data.

The original high reference is constructed correctly. Field Serre duality has the required index n−q, and positive Serre vanishing applies to the coherent canonical bundle over the original field. Taking a sufficiently large original integral very ample multiple M=dL makes every kr in the finite negative-twist list exceed the vanishing threshold. Flat field Čech base change preserves the list. Nothing here applies Noetherian Serre theory to C-circle. The list is empty when n=1.

The projective closure under that same original embedding has torsion-free affine coordinate rings, hence is flat over the valuation ring. BE's finite-presentation result applies to this model. After passing to the complete algebraically closed nontrivially valued C, BE4.18–20 give the finite integral closure and reduced special fiber. Smoothness makes the generic fiber normal, so the normalization changes no generic variety. Finite presentation applies again. The ample pullback uses the forward quasi-affine statement in Tag0892(2), whose hypotheses permit this non-Noetherian valuation ring. Projectivity is justified by the finite-morphism theorem. These steps preserve the original pulled-back bundle and sections.

In each model frame, the generating coefficients and a unit-ideal relation have norm at most one at every centered analytic point. The relation forces their maximum to be at least one. Consequently that maximum is exactly one everywhere, and the model metric is the same theta_C. This is an all-point assertion, not an assertion merely on the selected Shilov points. The original-field integral basis change is also valid: the finitely many bad residue vectors form proper subspaces over the infinite original residue field; a vector outside their union has a unit entry and admits an integral invertible completion. Applying the ultrametric inequality to the matrix and its integral inverse preserves the section maximum everywhere. S0 consequently has model norm one at every selected point.

The completion argument meets FK's actual hypotheses. R=C-circle is complete for the principal a-adic topology, and this topology has finite ideal type. Inverting a in each restricted-series ring gives the strict Tate algebra; boundedness of a convergent coefficient family proves the asserted identification directly. Its Noetherianity establishes topological universal Noetherianity outside (a). The complete printed FK0.8.4.1–5 units, including the proof of0.8.4.4, apply. The finite defining ideal is closed, its quotient is complete, and reduction modulo every a^j gives precisely the original polynomial presentation. Hence this is the actual chart completion and is topologically finitely presented. BE supplies its flatness and generic-domain identification. This proves no formal GAGA, global section-comparison theorem, or universal polarized-model realization.

The reduction argument is sound. GRW's dimension statements apply to the strict affinoid domains of smooth pure-dimensional X_C. Their canonical reductions are pure n-dimensional. The canonical-to-formal comparison is finite and surjective. Each source component has a closed image of the same dimension, because its function-field extension over that image is finite; these images cover the target. Therefore every actual residual component has dimension n. Over a generic formal point, finiteness and purity make the canonical points generic. GRW's generic-reduction correspondence then gives precisely finitely many Shilov points on each chart. A finite affine cover gives the finite nonempty set S, counting repeated chart occurrences once.

The reduction composition used in the manuscript is correctly typed: formal reduction equals the canonical-to-formal morphism composed after canonical reduction. The opposite composition printed in GM A.3 is a direction typo. I checked GM's pertinent appendix text independently; A.7's completed-algebraic-closure restriction is respected and is not applied to the transcendental Gauss extension. No singleton fiber is used to identify an entire residual field.

Poineau4.4 supplies residual transcendence degree n at each selected point. The manuscript's additional scheme-support argument is essential and correct: approximate independent unit-residue lifts inside the valued field of the original scheme support, with error below one. A polynomial relation over C, normalized by a coefficient of maximal norm, would reduce to a nonzero relation among the independent residues. Thus that scheme field has transcendence degree at least n, forcing original generic support. Only after this argument may H(y_i) be identified as the completion of honest C(X). Separately, the finite normalized component image on the original coordinate chart gives an original-coordinate residue subfield of transcendence degree n. Equality with the whole H-residue field is neither necessary nor asserted.

BE6.3(i) applies to every power of the same model bundle and every later global section. It therefore supplies the section supremum identity needed for all later FS families, rather than only for the initial embedding sections. Clearing denominators, taking section powers, adding arbitrary real constant weights, and commuting finite maxima with suprema preserve this norming identity.

The genuine reference support proof uses the correct CLDv1 units and hypotheses. The formal completion is flat, separated, and locally topologically finitely presented, with a finite affine cover. Its generic analytic space is good, separated, pure-dimensional, and boundaryless. For each point, the reduced closure W of its formal reduction is proper. CLD6.5.1 and6.6.8 identify the residual premodel using W and the restricted model bundle; its defining dimension is at most dim W. At nongeneric reductions this dimension is less than n. The lower-dimensional vanishing in6.8.3 and the support theorem6.9.2 therefore exclude those points from the top wedge. The support is contained in the same finite S. Dividing the integral-bundle wedge by d^n gives the rational reference. O supplies positivity, agreement with the genuine continuous operator, and total mass V. No individual atom coefficient, CLD6.9.3/4 formula, or inverse-curve measure is needed.

For n≥2, the full coefficient-Gauss construction is valid. On the n-dimensional original-coordinate image, coordinate differentials span the cotangent space at smooth points. The incidence differential has an identity block in the free coefficients and can have rank s=n−1 in the remaining block. A nonzero full minor proves generic full rank. Characteristic zero converts this rank into algebraic independence of all s(N+1) output coefficient residues. Maximal-coefficient reduction then proves the exact full Gauss norm for every coefficient polynomial; fractions and completion give isometric embeddings of the same F into every H'_i. Completion preserves residues and values by approximation with error strictly smaller than the norm of the element being approximated.

The generic hyperplanes cut an actual geometrically smooth curve. At a smooth e-dimensional point, vanishing and zero differential impose e+1 independent conditions. The bad incidence has dimension at most N−1, including the empty-incidence case, and its image is closed because the source variety is projective. An independent generic row avoids it. No positive-dimensional component is contained in the generic hyperplane, and an ample hyperplane section of such a projective component is nonempty. Repeating the independent rows gives a regular sequence and the asserted smooth curve.

The Koszul calculation checks both required diagonals. In complex degree −k, the total-zero term is H^k(O(−kM)), and an incoming total-minus-one term is H^(k−1)(O(−kM)). The chosen vanishings kill both, with negative ample H0=0 handling k=1. The latter follows from the displayed multiplication injection and the fact that a positive-dimensional very ample bundle has at least two independent sections. There is no outgoing differential into positive complex degree. Finite affine Čech complexes commute with every flat field extension, so H0(O_D)=the base field also after geometric extension and completion. A smooth geometric projective curve has disjoint irreducible components; the absence of nontrivial global idempotents makes it connected and hence integral. Its actual restricted rational bundle has raw degree a=d^(n−1)V.

The evaluated curve points have generic scheme support before any F(D) embedding is invoked. Their residue contains the original coordinate subfield and the independent free residues, of transcendence degree n+sN over the original residue field. The full coefficient base has degree s(N+1), leaving relative transcendence degree at least one. Closed curve support would give a finite scheme-field extension and an algebraic valued residue extension, contradicting that lower bound. Now F(D) embeds honestly. Original C(X) and the free coefficients lie in its image; finite coefficient approximation in numerators and nonzero denominators proves density in H'_i and gives relative residual transcendence degree exactly one.

The value argument is also correct. Independent residues and rationally independent values yield algebraically independent elements by grouping polynomial terms by value classes. The original n independent residues exhaust the dimension of C(X), so the relative rational value rank is zero. Divisibility of C's value group eliminates a nontrivial ordered torsion extension. Unit Gauss variables and completion add no values. The algebraic-closure embeddings are isometric over complete F, and completion extends them to B and Omega_i. Algebraic extensions have algebraic residue extensions; completion changes no residues. A transcendental residue lifted from F(D) therefore remains transcendental over the algebraic extension of the base residue field. This proves generic support for z_i before invoking B(D), and yields the stated type-II invariants. It does not imply H(z_i)=Omega_i. Every original rational-function value, and therefore every original section value in the pulled-back reference, is preserved. For n=1, the direct use of X_C and y_i establishes the same assertions without incidence.

The completed algebraic closures used here are genuinely algebraically closed. This standard fact can also be checked directly: approximate the coefficients of a monic polynomial by coefficients in the algebraic closure, keep all roots uniformly bounded, and successively choose roots whose distances are bounded by a suitable root of the coefficient error using the product formula for polynomial evaluation. Errors tending sufficiently rapidly to zero give a Cauchy sequence of roots; its limit is a root in the completion. Repeating after division proves algebraic closedness. Thus the actual fields used in the normalization and stable-reduction applications satisfy their hypotheses.

BPR4.22 applies to the actual smooth geometrically integral projective curve over complete algebraically closed nontrivially real-valued B. Its printed proof explicitly accommodates rank-one non-Noetherian valuation rings. BPR3.13 includes the finite type-II set and permits later punctured refinements while retaining the old metric skeleton. The construction fixes that skeleton and D0 before any later FS family and retains every cycle. No universal realization of graph or polarization data is imported.

Lemma 3 is correct without spherical completeness. The induction proves equivalence with the maximum coordinate norm on each finite-dimensional completed-base span. A preceding complete span is closed; a vector outside it has positive distance from it, giving exactly the two displayed estimates. The resulting closed span contains dense E and therefore equals its completion. Independent residue unit lifts remain linearly independent by maximal-coefficient normalization, giving the residue-degree bound. Neither defectlessness nor equality in a fundamental inequality is asserted.

For a nonconstant f=t/S0^k, the coefficientwise pole bound gives degree at most k deg(M_D)=kd a. The normal-curve extension, finiteness, flatness, effective Cartier degree, and pullback degree statements apply over the actual field B. Constants have slope zero. After deleting zeros and poles, the function is an annular unit. At value-group radii, the Laurent reductions of the unit and its inverse are inverse monomials; dominance cannot switch through a tie. Convergence on a compact strict subannulus gives the strict error bound in the displayed monomial form. The actual Gauss residue field is B-tilde(tau). For q≠0, maximal-coefficient reduction identifies the completed B(f) residue subfield as B-tilde(tau^q), of index |q|. Lemma3 bounds that index by the honest function-field degree. Dense value-group radii and continuity extend the estimate to type-III points and endpoints. Integrating along the retained old paths gives the stated slope estimate.

Every original nonzero defining section stays nonzero on the curve because its original generic value is preserved. Dividing the entire weighted maximum, including every real weight, by kd gives the a-Lipschitz bound. The reference frame has weight zero at the selected points. Same-reference norming supplies one zero value for each normalized FS scalar, so all its selected values lie in [−aD0,0]. Compact directed closed-superlevel sets prove that the suprema of any actual decreasing FS net decrease to the actual endpoint supremum. Passing the finite point bounds therefore works before E1 membership. Genuine atomic support and O's raw pushforward give M0=VaD0 for all normalized actual nontrivial psh endpoints. When n=1 this retains the raw V² factor. Trivial valuations use precisely T's canonical zero-moment reference.

Lemma 4 is correct without a common finite-valued anchor. The summable convex sums are actual E1 potentials, decrease, and have energy at least −1. Extended majorant energy is used before asserting endpoint nontriviality or finite energy. An identically −∞ endpoint would put a tail below −R for any chosen R; taking R>1/V contradicts the energy lower bound. The nontrivial endpoint is consequently E1 by decreasing energy continuity. Sequential monotone convergence then gives the divergent target integral. Conversely, positive linear scaling into the unit-cost set proves all-test integrability from finite U. Finite constant shifts supply absolute integrability.

Lemma 5 proves the precise Radon-net law required here. Strict open superlevels form directed unions; compact inner approximation and finite subcovers supply one common stage. A common stage also handles finitely many layers, after which height truncation and layer refinement recover the full integral. This establishes the law for continuous/lower-semicontinuous increasing nets, without using arbitrary measurable-net monotone convergence. The finite continuous-dual bound excludes an infinite endpoint integral. O's decreasing energy law then proves equality of continuous and all-E1 dual suprema.

Lemma 6 uses O's genuine actual segment polynomial correctly. All A_k are finite and nonnegative, their sum is (n+1)B, and A0≤M0. The positive-index Bernstein weights are bounded by their sum 1−(1−s)^n≤ns. Integration gives D_n=n(n+1)/2 for every real t in [0,1], with zero coefficients omitted at poles. The explicit positive scale makes both contributions to B(tu) at most 1/2. Under finite U, this proves inequalities2.2–4, including the completed-square dual bound. Combining Lemmas4–6 proves Theorem2's equivalence. Reference covariance uses only a bounded scalar change and the energy cocycle; it does not transfer the old atomic support to an arbitrary new reference.

Proposition 7 is a valid supporting argument for an already known genuine output. O gives mass, integrability, concavity, and the finite initial segment derivative on a common finite-value full-measure set. The supporting inequality proves maximization over actual E1; Lemma5 identifies its value with the continuous dual. It constructs no inverse solution. For intrinsic finite targets, solving the quadratic inequality in sqrt(B) on a maximizing tail with F≥−1 gives10.1 exactly. That bound establishes no compactness or actual realization. Product limits, norm completions, and weak compactness of measures do not supply the missing psh endpoints, outer both-sign differentiation, orthogonality, or all-point uniqueness.

All six exact notes agree with these mathematical scopes: n1 retains the grants and failed data; n2 records the same-reference model and support construction; n3 records the actual common curve and moment argument; n4 retains the material finite-U repair and genuine counterexample; n5 distinguishes known-output maximization from inverse existence; n6 limits finite checks and provenance claims to their recorded roles. The quote-free ledger was checked against the retrieved primary units rather than accepted as certification. Builds, hashes, read flags, grids, reproduction bindings, and operational statements were not used as mathematical premises. The worker's statement about not invoking Xean does not establish a model switch or alter the supplied ROOT binding.

Harmless clarifications are limited to reading component notation on the S0 chart as the corresponding nonempty component open, counting repeated chart points once, and choosing R>1/V in the constant-tail contradiction. GM A.3's composition direction is already corrected in the manuscript. In Tag0B3I's affine-chart proof, the inhomogeneous coordinate map lands in A; the printed symmetric-algebra target there is an evident typo, and the closed-immersion argument is verified with the actual evaluation map. None changes a conclusion or supplies a missing hypothesis. Finite U is expressly not classified as harmless.

The full pertinent immediate printed units and their proofs were retrieved for the essential external premises below. This audit does not claim a fresh reconstruction of every recursively cited book foundation. Review198's unresolved direct-formal source premises14/15 are not antecedents of this manuscript. The literature-discovery abstracts remain scope data, without an absence-of-literature assertion. No essential premise of the present partial argument remains unresolved.

passages.statement: For a smooth proper pure n-dimensional scheme X over a field k, an invertible sheaf A, and integers r and 0≤q≤n, Serre duality gives H^q(X,A^(−r))^∨ ≅ H^(n−q)(X,ω_X⊗A^r), where ω_X=∧^nΩ_(X/k) (Stacks48.27.1(5),(7), Tag0FVV).
If R is Noetherian, X is proper over R, L is ample invertible, and F is coherent, then H^p(X,F⊗L^d)=0 for every p>0 and all sufficiently large d (Stacks30.16.1(4), Tag0B5T).

Over a complete nontrivially valued real-valued non-Archimedean field K, a separated flat finite-type K-circle scheme model is finitely presented; its completion with respect to a nonzero topologically nilpotent element is flat and topologically of finite type, and its formal generic fiber identifies with the analytic domain of points centered on the model. For a proper model that domain is the whole analytification (BE1805.01016v3,4.3–4.6).

For a proper model that domain is the whole analytification (BE1805.01016v3,4.3–4.6).
passages.quote: flat and topologically of finite type

passages.statement: Let C be a complete algebraically closed nontrivially valued non-Archimedean field, X a reduced finite-type C-scheme, and mathcal X a scheme model of X. The integral closure of mathcal X in X is finite over mathcal X, is again a model of X, and has reduced special fiber (BE1805.01016v3,4.18–4.20).
For a quasi-affine morphism f:X→Y of schemes and an ample invertible sheaf M on Y, f^*M is ample on X; no Noetherian hypothesis is required (Stacks29.38.7(2), Tag0892).
passages.quote: If $\mathcal{M}$ is ample and $f$ quasi-affine, then $f^*\mathcal{M}$ is ample.

passages.statement: A finite morphism of schemes is projective (Stacks Tag0B3I).

A classical affinoid algebra over the fraction field of an a-adically complete valuation ring V, with 0≠a in its maximal ideal, is Noetherian; in particular the strict Tate algebra V⟨T1,…,Tm⟩[1/a] is Noetherian (FK1308.4734v5,0.9.3.1–2).
passages.quote: Any classical affinoid algebra is a Noetherian ring.

passages.statement: If (R,I) is a complete pair of finite ideal type and R is topologically universally Noetherian outside I, every ideal of every restricted-series ring R⟨T1,…,Tm⟩ is closed, and its quotient is complete. Topological finite presentation means presentation by a finitely generated ideal in such a restricted-series ring (FK1308.4734v5,0.8.4.1–5).

Analytification preserves dimension and equidimension of finite-type schemes over a complete non-Archimedean field. For a strictly affinoid equidimensional space over a complete nontrivially valued field, canonical reduction preserves its dimension and equidimension (GRW2017 publisher version,2.4 and2.10).

For an affine admissible formal model over a complete nontrivially valued field, its strict affinoid canonical reduction maps finitely and surjectively to the formal special fiber. Canonical reduction is surjective; each generic canonical-reduction point has one inverse analytic point, and the inverse image of all generic points is exactly the finite Shilov boundary. Formal reduction is canonical reduction followed by the canonical-to-formal morphism (GRW2017 publisher version,2.12 and2.14–2.17).

passages.statement: If x belongs to the Shilov boundary of a strictly k-affinoid space X over a complete non-Archimedean field k, then trdeg_(k-tilde) H(x)-tilde equals the local analytic dimension dim_(k,x)(X) (Poineau2013 publisher version,Lemma4.4).

For a line-bundle model on a projective scheme model over a complete non-Archimedean field, the associated model-metric supremum of every global section equals its maximum on the model's finite Shilov set (BE1805.01016v3,Lemma6.3(i)).

Let mathcal X be a flat separated formal k-circle scheme with a locally finite affine cover topologically of finite presentation, x a point of its generic fiber, and W the reduced closure of its reduction in the special fiber. The germ reduction is described by W; x is interior exactly when W is proper. For a formally metrized bundle E, (W,E|W) is a residual premodel. If W is proper, the defining dimension is at most dim W (CLD1204.6277v1,6.5.1,6.6.8 and6.7.2).

On a good separated pure n-dimensional analytic space, the top mixed wedge of PL metrized line bundles is supported at points where their simultaneous residual defining dimension is n; its boundary coefficients vanish. Lower defining dimension gives local zero top wedge. On a compact carrier the resulting discrete support is finite (CLD1204.6277v1,6.7.3,6.8.3 and6.9.1–2).
passages.quote: est nulle au voisinage de x.

Lower defining dimension gives local zero top wedge. On a compact carrier the resulting discrete support is finite (CLD1204.6277v1,6.7.3,6.8.3 and6.9.1–2).

A smooth connected projective curve over a complete algebraically closed nontrivially real-valued non-Archimedean field admits a semistable vertex set and compact connected metric skeleton. Any finite set of type-II points can be included. After deleting finitely many algebraic points, a containing semistable vertex set gives a refinement retaining the old skeleton and its metric lengths (BPR1404.0279v1,3.13 and4.22, with its standing field hypotheses).
passages.quote: There exists a semistable vertex set of X.

passages.statement: Over a complete algebraically closed nontrivially valued real-valued field B, a unit on a strict closed standard annulus has form cT^q(1+g), with c∈B*, q∈Z and supremum norm of g less than one. Annular Gauss norms evaluate Laurent series by the maximum of |c_m|ρ^m, and skeletal path length is logarithmic radius difference (BPR1404.0279v1,2.1–2.3).

A rational map from a normal curve over a field to a proper variety extends to a morphism. A nonconstant morphism of proper integral curves is finite, and it is flat if the target is normal (Stacks53.2.1–4, Tag0BXX).
passages.quote: If $Y$ is normal, then $f$ is flat.

passages.statement: A rational map from a normal curve over a field to a proper variety extends to a morphism. A nonconstant morphism of proper integral curves is finite, and it is flat if the target is normal (Stacks53.2.1–4, Tag0BXX).

For a proper scheme X of dimension at most one over a field k, an effective Cartier divisor D is finite of degree dim_kΓ(D,O_D); for a locally free sheaf E of rank r, deg(E(D))=r deg(D)+deg(E) (Stacks33.44.9, Tag0AYY).
For a nonconstant morphism f:X→Y of proper integral curves over a field and a locally free sheaf E on Y, deg(f^*E)=[k(X):k(Y)]deg(E) (Stacks33.44.11, Tag0AYZ).

For a bounded metric φ on a semiample rational line bundle, the regular psh envelope Q(φ) is the pointwise limit of m^(-1)FS(mφ), and convergence is uniform if and only if Q(φ) is continuous; continuity of envelopes is a separate hypothesis (BE1805.01016v3,7.24–7.30).

GM AppendixA.7's preservation of divisorial points under scalar extension assumes the extension field is a subfield of the completed algebraic closure of the original field; it does not assert this for arbitrary transcendental extensions.
Reboulet's arbitrary-field finite-energy geodesic result assumes continuity of envelopes (arXiv:2012.07972).
The degeneration result at https://jep.centre-mersenne.org/articles/10.5802/jep.229/ is a result for degenerating complex projective families and their non-Archimedean space over C((t)).
passages.quote: degenerating families of complex projective manifolds

passages.statement: For an analytic curve over a complete algebraically closed nontrivially valued field, a generic point with residual transcendence degree one and relative rational value rank zero is type II; skeletal points have types II or III.
The completion of an algebraic closure of a complete real-valued non-Archimedean field is algebraically closed.
Completion of a valued field changes neither its value group nor its residue field.
A nongeneric scheme point of an integral curve of finite type over a field is closed and has finite scheme residue field over that base.
A complete valued field is henselian, so its absolute value extends uniquely to any algebraic extension.
passages.quote: Every complete valued field is henselian.

passages.statement: A torsion-free module over a valuation ring is flat.

In characteristic zero, a finitely generated field extension has a separating transcendence basis, and the rank of the differentials of finitely many elements equals the transcendence degree of the subfield they generate.

The germ reduction is described by W; x is interior exactly when W is proper. For a formally metrized bundle E, (W,E|W) is a residual premodel. If W is proper, the defining dimension is at most dim W (CLD1204.6277v1,6.5.1,6.6.8 and6.7.2).

On a good separated pure n-dimensional analytic space, the top mixed wedge of PL metrized line bundles is supported at points where their simultaneous residual defining dimension is n; its boundary coefficients vanish. Lower defining dimension gives local zero top wedge. On a compact carrier the resulting discrete support is finite (CLD1204.6277v1,6.7.3,6.8.3 and6.9.1–2).

A smooth connected projective curve over a complete algebraically closed nontrivially real-valued non-Archimedean field admits a semistable vertex set and compact connected metric skeleton. Any finite set of type-II points can be included. After deleting finitely many algebraic points, a containing semistable vertex set gives a refinement retaining the old skeleton and its metric lengths (BPR1404.0279v1,3.13 and4.22, with its standing field hypotheses).

Over a complete algebraically closed nontrivially valued real-valued field B, a unit on a strict closed standard annulus has form cT^q(1+g), with c∈B*, q∈Z and supremum norm of g less than one. Annular Gauss norms evaluate Laurent series by the maximum of |c_m|ρ^m, and skeletal path length is logarithmic radius difference (BPR1404.0279v1,2.1–2.3).

A rational map from a normal curve over a field to a proper variety extends to a morphism. A nonconstant morphism of proper integral curves is finite, and it is flat if the target is normal (Stacks53.2.1–4, Tag0BXX).

For a proper scheme X of dimension at most one over a field k, an effective Cartier divisor D is finite of degree dim_kΓ(D,O_D); for a locally free sheaf E of rank r, deg(E(D))=r deg(D)+deg(E) (Stacks33.44.9, Tag0AYY).
For a nonconstant morphism f:X→Y of proper integral curves over a field and a locally free sheaf E on Y, deg(f^*E)=[k(X):k(Y)]deg(E) (Stacks33.44.11, Tag0AYZ).

For a bounded metric φ on a semiample rational line bundle, the regular psh envelope Q(φ) is the pointwise limit of m^(-1)FS(mφ), and convergence is uniform if and only if Q(φ) is continuous; continuity of envelopes is a separate hypothesis (BE1805.01016v3,7.24–7.30).

GM AppendixA.7's preservation of divisorial points under scalar extension assumes the extension field is a subfield of the completed algebraic closure of the original field; it does not assert this for arbitrary transcendental extensions.
Reboulet's arbitrary-field finite-energy geodesic result assumes continuity of envelopes (arXiv:2012.07972).
The degeneration result at https://jep.centre-mersenne.org/articles/10.5802/jep.229/ is a result for degenerating complex projective families and their non-Archimedean space over C((t)).

For an analytic curve over a complete algebraically closed nontrivially valued field, a generic point with residual transcendence degree one and relative rational value rank zero is type II; skeletal points have types II or III.
The completion of an algebraic closure of a complete real-valued non-Archimedean field is algebraically closed.
Completion of a valued field changes neither its value group nor its residue field.
A nongeneric scheme point of an integral curve of finite type over a field is closed and has finite scheme residue field over that base.
A complete valued field is henselian, so its absolute value extends uniquely to any algebraic extension.
A torsion-free module over a valuation ring is flat.

In characteristic zero, a finitely generated field extension has a separating transcendence basis, and the rank of the differentials of finitely many elements equals the transcendence degree of the subfield they generate.
